name: Earn Trust
definition: Leaders listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. They are vocally self-critical, even when doing so is awkward or embarrassing. They do not believe they, or their team, smell like roses. They benchmark themselves and their teams against the best.

rows.under: Portrays an image of never being wrong. Hides the miss or blames the weather.
rows.justRight: Takes responsibility for what they or the team did not deliver, names the cause, and says what changes.
rows.over: Is so self-deprecating that it reads as a lack of confidence, or as a performance.

rows.under: Defends the team past the point of honesty, or refuses to accept any responsibility.
rows.justRight: Owns the miss upward without naming individuals as the problem. Gives the team the real feedback in private.
rows.over: Throws the team under the bus to protect a personal reputation.

rows.situation: When a problem is still small
rows.under: Covers the problem and discourages sharing. Blind spots grow, and the same error repeats.
rows.justRight: Is honest about team performance. Surfaces the real shortfall while it is still cheap to fix.
rows.over: Is self-critical about trivia, or dwells until morale and confidence collapse.

rows.under: Does not listen. Talks over critics. Treats disagreement as disloyalty.
rows.justRight: Listens all the way through, speaks candidly, and changes the plan when the other person is right.
rows.over: Agrees with everyone in the room so nobody is upset, and the decision is mush.

rows.under: Arrogant and disrespectful. Builds walls. Questions motives instead of the work.
rows.justRight: Treats peers as colleagues on the same customer problem. Uses data to settle the conflict and gives credit when another team carried it.
rows.over: Spends the week on lunches and relationship theater, and the deliverable slips.

rows.under: Makes a soft promise, hedges, or stays vague so nobody can say they missed.
rows.justRight: Makes a hard, clear promise and keeps it. If they cannot keep it, they say so early and repair it.
rows.over: Promises anything to be liked, then burns trust when the thing does not arrive.

rows.under: Hides behind another team, a system, or an act of God.
rows.justRight: Calls it like it is, on their team or someone else's. Names the miss, names the fix, and moves.
rows.over: Takes blame they do not own in order to keep a relationship, and the root cause stays unfixed.

rows.situation: When comparing the team to the best
rows.under: Assumes the team is already the best. Unapproachable. No intensity on getting better.
rows.justRight: Benchmarks against the best, shows the gap, and stays approachable enough that people will bring the next gap to them.
rows.over: Publishes only the failures. Other teams start to doubt the group can {lp:deliver-results}.

rows.situation: When the team needs the truth
rows.under: Accepts that the team failed and then blames the people below. Avoids the hard conversation.
rows.justRight: Owns the problem as the leader, seeks the pain points, and still gives clear, tough feedback with a standard attached.
rows.over: Protects the team from every hard word, or points out every fault until nobody will take a risk.

rows.situation: When it would be easy to be clever
rows.under: Wins the room by being clever at someone else's expense. Escalates past a person they have not spoken to.
rows.justRight: Is kind without being soft. Talks to the person first. Optimizes for the customer and the company, not a personal scoreboard.
rows.over: Makes being liked the goal. Will not risk a relationship even when the customer is losing.
